package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The content is a high-level overview of software supply chain security risks, dependency management, and best practices, not an analysis of a particular malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Use of dependencies from unverified or unknown sources (SOUP)
Frequent updates or changes to transitive dependencies without clear justification
Introduction of new dependencies with similar names to popular packages (typosquatting)
Automated or social engineering attempts to inject code into open source repositories
file_indicators: Dependencies with names similar to popular packages (e.g., one character off)
Unusual or unreviewed binaries included in project directories
Unpinned dependency versions in manifest files (e.g., package.json, requirements.txt)
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound requests during build or install phases
Connections to domains not associated with official package repositories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor dependency manifests for unpinned or suspiciously named packages. Use SCA tools to analyze both direct and transitive dependencies for vulnerabilities and provenance. Watch for unexpected network activity during build, install, or runtime phases. Regularly review and audit all third-party components, and enforce policies requiring known provenance for all dependencies.
